readings.text: A13.15 steps 5 and 7, "refuses uncommitted changes": run_claims_phase4's git_state (git status --porcelain --no-renames over the system folder and the reference folders of Hyperbolic Oracles and Engram Mind's Eye, untracked files one by one, renames counting both paths) must list nothing but the step's own outputs; a sys.path entry inside the repository outside that scope is refused. The check, HEAD included, is repeated before each pool and before writing (git_checks). --allow-dirty exists for the dry run only and marks its record.

A13.15 step 7, "it resumes at the same HEAD from its finished jobs": a runs.jsonl line is reused only at the same HEAD and configuration signature (mode, shape, the pins, WordNet, epochs, burn-in, the seeds and the SHA-256 of the runner and lexicon modules), and only while every file it names still has its recorded SHA-256; anything else is rerun. Every start is listed with its environment and load average.

A13.8, the value stream: for certified forms the 120-digit Decimal's str(); for exact keys (Sym, the distance-only score, GloVe's key, WN and the word-tree integers) the key's str() (an int or "p/q"); for the reported uncertified forms (NK17, the product) the 120-digit Decimal's str(). A direction file streams each row's forward then reverse value; a HiT file streams each row's slots in slot order.

A13.14, itemScoresSha: the SHA-256 of the code file's uncompressed TSV bytes (gzip's bytes depend on the zlib build); the gzip file's own SHA-256 is the one checked before pass 2 reads it, and both are in stage2-manifest.json.

A13.14, scoreForm and senseRule fields (ASCII): G, Grev (Phi_G(y, x), L12 control 3), DepG (Dep°: Dep at G's senses), Dep, Sym, Groot, dist (the distance-only score), cos (GloVe), LCh, NK17, product; max, first, gensim; "-" where no senses are read (HiT, GloVe).

Spec section 0, "four worker processes at most": --workers is refused above 4; the replay shares the training pool, longest job first (A10's scheduling), so "a fifth slot when a core frees" is a slot of the same four.

A13.16 with spec section 16, the projection: tuning (12 runs per cell) and decisive training (5 measured and 5 edge-shuffled runs per cell, the two pre-flight jobs) from the measured per-epoch wall times of two epochs per cell with four processes at once (lr 1, seeds 95500-95503), the two 1,000-epoch replays from a two-epoch replay (seed 95504), the projection's own wall time, and A13.16's estimates for the exact arms (0.5 h), the two evaluations (0.1 h, 0.6 h) and the dry run (1.0 h); the total is compared with 11 h. The disk projection is the code-file lines x 6 B plus every table (float .npy and snapped text).

A13.14, instanceId "names set, pin and slice": the instance manifest's names, with -at (L14(b), U_@), -glove (L15(b), L13 control 3), -dir (BD-dir), -random/-hard (HiT's settings) and -relabelled (L14 control 2) for the slices; the dry sets are named by their pins too (hyperlex-ccb4161-verbs, ...), and the dry split and HIT-R, built from WordNet, by wordnet30-verb-at-split-<val|test> and hit-r-wordnet30-noun-at-<...>, with the SHA-256 of their slot lines as instanceSha.

A13.13, the dry run names fewer sets than the registered decisions read: each decided slot without its own dry set takes the nearest dry set, marked stand-in: L13(b)'s WB takes the HyperLex verb detection set (clusters by word1), L15(a)'s MEN takes MEN's v-v rows (named for (b)), L15(b)'s WSR takes SimLex's verbs within GloVe; all sealed. G_root is not read in the dry run (no entity.n.01 among the verbs).
A13.13, the dry split: hit.hit_r on the verb @ graph with Rng(4500)-Rng(4502) and its default n_val = floor(0.05 |T|) (1,092 for 21,840 indirect pairs).

A13.11, F1 under HiT's protocol (measured tables only), with A13.8 ("pass 2 ... computes every metric from pass 1's files alone") and A13.6 (one tie-class list "where a metric compares" values): the measured table's pass-1 job writes one code file of HiT val's and HiT test's G values together (val rows, then test rows, 21 slots, keyed val:<row> and test:<row>; its value-stream SHA-256 and side file as for every code file); pass 2 reads it after its SHA-256 check and computes F1 per setting (slot 0 the positive, the setting's other slots the negatives): theta the val code with the best val F1, ties to the smallest, a pair positive when its code is at least theta (stats2.f1_threshold); it decides nothing and has no LBENCH/1 record.

A13.15 step 7 with A10.14, "the same run": a restart that finds every tuning job finished and tuning-stage2.json already holding exactly these runs, files and choice leaves it and its settings unchanged.
Spec section 10, settings-stage2.json: the two geometry keys of the spec, each d a grid string or null, plus "tuning" naming tuning-stage2.json (path, HEAD, SHA-256) as A10.8's settings.json did.

A13.10.6, the tuning tables kept in the cache for controls 1-2: a missing one (or one whose snapped text lost its SHA-256) stops the decisive run; A10.9's retraining of a lost tuning table is not carried over, since A13 does not register it.
A13 L13 control 3: an empty GloVe direction set (no True row within GloVe) is recorded as accuracy 0 with a flag; it cannot occur on the registered data.
A13 L14, presence and the decision rules: the seeds are indexed j = 0..4 (the training seed s itself in the registered run, 3000 + j in the dry run).

A13.3, the morphy rule ("only for words absent raw"): every HL pair-set word is in the index raw, so on HL the morphy rule's scores are the maximum's and are not recomputed; the number of HL words absent raw is recorded.

Spec section 8, the relabelling tail and |dRR|: G in binary64 by numpy's vectorised arccosh and sqrt (math.acosh may differ in the last bits; sqrt is correctly rounded in both), ties pessimistic; reported only.

A13.11, "the closure bit computed from WordNet in pass 1": some sense pairing (s, t) with t a strict @/@i ancestor of s (wngraph.WNGraph.anc), senses in the instance's universe, per row of every scored word-pair instance, in each direction.
A13.7, the strongest permutation of a control: the largest point estimate of the permuted arm's own metric (rho, AP or direction accuracy, exact), ties to the smaller i; then one interval.

Spec section 0, the load average every 10 minutes: sampled at every start, at each phase's start and end, and while a pool waits (polled at most every 60 s, a sample once 10 minutes have passed); no thread, since a fork pool must not fork a process with a second thread.

A13.8, BD and BD-dir: the detection AP reads a tie-class list of the forward values alone, BD-dir one list of forward and reverse values of every covered row (both written by one pass-1 job from the same certified values); pass 2 selects the True rows (the dry run: TYPE hyp-1 to hyp-4).

A13.11, Nickel & Kiela 2018's diagnostic: rho (exact, average ranks) between r and sp/(sp + lp) over the nodes of U_@ (the dry run: the verb @ graph), sp the distance to the nearest root and lp the height, both on E (senses.sp_lp); r is ordered by |n|^2 for a learned table and by x0 for H3 and H2, read on the same nodes; "the tables" are every learned table of the run (tuning, measured, edge-shuffled, floors).

A13.11, "NK17 scores" (L14): each measured table scored by NK17 (A13.5, alpha 10^3, 120 digits, uncertified) on HiT test (21 slots: mean RR in both settings) and on HL within U_@ (rho), deciding nothing. One rule for every table without x0: a flat table (the learned Euclidean table, and the exact flat arms F3, F3*, F2, F2* in the L12 grid), which has no Poincare norm, is read with its Euclidean norm and distance (scores2.nk17_value), as P17 scored its Euclidean embeddings by eq. 8; named for the definitions amendment.

A13.11, "L14's tables on these rows" (L13): the measured tables read by G at o on BD, WB and BD-dir covered in U_@ (BD-at, WB-at, BD-dir-at; senses in U_@, as L14(b) reads HL), detection AP (pessimistic and sklearn's convention) and direction accuracy on the True rows, with the exact Lorentz - Euclidean differences per (d, seed); no interval. The instance manifest records the two U_@ pair sets.

A13.11, the suite's own detection protocol (L13): BD-suite and WB-suite hold the covered rows of the val and test folds in one tie-class list per arm (the six and WN, G with the maximum over senses); a test row the arm does not cover takes the code of its lowest in-vocabulary validation score (it ties with that class), and AP is taken over the whole test fold, pessimistic and in sklearn's convention (stats2.suite_detection); with no in-vocabulary validation row the lowest in-vocabulary test code stands in (flagged). The dry sets have no validation fold, so it does not run there.

A13.11, "the vocabulary each arm misses": per word-pair instance and per vocabulary an arm reads (the senses in the instance's universe; index.<pos> for W; GloVe 6B's words for GloVe), the word types of the rows the word-level selection kept that it misses, as a count, the SHA-256 of their N_S forms in code-point order and the rows holding one; no word is written (A13.2).

A13.11, "H3 against the learned tables on HL within U_@": rho(H3 G) - rho(table G) on HL-at for each measured table, with the word-level ci_rho and the row bootstrap beside it, as every difference of rho (A13.7); deciding nothing.

A13 L15 control 2, "for every arm and set": every arm of L15's Arms list on the sets it reads: on SL and MEN the six exact arms and the controls K3, S-full_i and W_i (each of the 20 permutations an arm, as A13.4 defines them), all with Sym; on MEN, WSR and HL within GloVe, H3 with Sym and GloVe 300-d. The readings the Arms list marks as reported (H3 with G against GloVe on HL; GloVe at 50-d) decide nothing and are not banded. stats2.decide_l15 refuses a control 2 that lacks one of these (arm, set) pairs.

A13's notation, "the definitions amendment is the dated amendment of item 15 step 4 (Amendment 14 unless another comes first)", with A13.2, "freezes it by its SHA-256": registered tuning and the decisive run find it as the earliest amendment after 13 whose text holds the instance manifest's SHA-256; a later amendment (the lr-freeze amendment, an erratum) may restate that hash. A11.4's exactly-one rule is kept for the lr-freeze amendment and settings-stage2.json only, as A13's notation registers it.

A13.2, "parsing runs under python3 -B -I with explicit paths": --time, --dry, --tune and --decisive refuse an interpreter without -B and -I (sys.flags); the runner puts its own folder on sys.path, and the spawn pool passes both flags on to its workers. The self-test (a synthetic world) and --write-settings (this project's own JSON) parse nothing fetched and are not held to it. Every start records the flags.

A13.8 and A13.11, the reported values that A13 defines outside pass 1's files of tie-class codes of an (instance, arm, form, rule, table): the 200 relabelled tails (L14 control 2, "computed in binary64"), |dRR| (against float64 scoring of the unsnapped table as stored), Nickel & Kiela 2018's diagnostic and the radius ranks of the seven labels under P (over WordNet's nodes, no Stage-2 row) are computed in pass 2 from the tables, each read only after its float or snapped SHA-256 matches the run record; none reads a gold, label or TYPE field, and each decides nothing. Named for the definitions amendment, since A13.8 says pass 2 computes every metric from pass 1's files alone.

A13.11 (L12), "every arm under every score of item 5 and every sense rule of item 3" (L12_GRID): A13.11's L12 grid is L12's 48 arms (A13 L12, Arms: the six exact trees, WN, K3 and each S-full_i and each W_i, i < 20) x 7 scores x 4 sense rules = 1,344 cells, each scored, an alias or n/a; each S-full_i and W_i places words on H3's points, so every form reads it as it reads K3 (A13.4's geometric arm: one hyperboloid table). S3's 5 arms and the chain's 3 (WN-U, ST, the letter tree) stay at G with the maximum (at 841b90c the grid had 8 arms and 224 cells, and S-full_i and W_i also stayed at G with the maximum; Amendment 14, items 5 and 6). The scores are G, Sym, Dep°, Dep and the reported NK17 (the 47 geometric arms: Poincaré norms on H3, H2, K3, S-full_i and W_i, Euclidean norms on the exact flat arms, READING stage2-runner-25), product (the 47 geometric arms) and WN-LCh (WN); the rules are the maximum, first senses, gensim's rule and noun morphy. A cell is scored, an alias of a cell equal to it by definition (morphy = the maximum, since every pair-set word is in the index raw; Dep° under first senses or gensim's rule = Dep under that rule, G's pair being the rule's; Sym and WN-LCh under gensim's rule = the maximum, the gensim pair having the least distance), or n/a with its reason; reported.L12.grid lists all 1,344 cells (48 arms x 7 scores x 4 rules).

A13.3, gensim's rule on WN (scores2.WNScorer.gensim_pair): WN has no geometry, so "the sense pair at the smallest distance" uses its path p (WN-path, Sym_WN = -p): the pair of the largest Sym_WN, ties to the first in (i, j) order, then G_WN or Dep_WN of that pair.

A13.11 (L13), "WN and GloVe": WN by G_WN with the maximum over senses on BD, WB (detection AP) and BD-dir (direction accuracy); GloVe 300-d's cosine detection AP on BD-glove and WB-glove, BD's and WB's rows covered in U_full with both N_S words in GloVe's vocabulary (A13.3; the instance manifest's gloveCovered rows, which manifest_check compares), clusters as the base set's; GloVe's direction on BD-dir-glove is L13 control 3's file. Reported.

A13.11, "the closure membership of every scored pair (from WordNet, in pass 1)", and L12's "the closure bit computed from WordNet in pass 1": the bits of closure_bits (READING stage2-runner-20) for every scored word-pair instance (HL, BD, whose rows BD-dir scores both ways, WB, and every other set of L12, L13, L15 and A13.11, senses in the instance's universe) are written in pass 1 as code files (row, forward bit, reverse bit; write_bits_files) with their SHA-256s in the run record, and pass 2 reads them only through that check. Reported per row as one character per pair-set row, forward + 2 x reverse, with the pair set's pairSetSha; no word is written. The non-closure positives (AP on BD and on WB, direction on BD-dir) are the True rows whose forward bit is 0, with every negative.

A13 L14 Instances (b), "the number of HL rows that are E edges for some sense pairing": on HL-at with senses in U_@ (edge_bits, pass 1, a bits file like the closure bits), the rows with some sense pair (s, t) in E, x the child (forward: the number); the rows with (t, s) in E, either, and the counts by TYPE (pass 2) beside it.

A13 L14 Risks, the sign agreement of G_root and the distance-only score with G: per (d, setting) on HiT test, and per d on HL-at, the seeds at which the form's Lorentz - Euclidean estimate and G's (on HL-at: L14(b)'s own interval at that seed) are not both > 0 or both <= 0; three or more such seeds are flagged "stated".

A13.11's diagnostic, "WN-LCh's tie classes against WN-path's on every set": WN-LCh is scored (with the maximum over senses) wherever WN-path is read: HL (and its first-senses cell of the grid), SL, WSS, WSC and WSR; per set, whether the two tie-class lists are equal, their class counts and both rhos.

The wiring (it implements A13's Decision, Metric and Controls lines as written): every decided comparison and control of L12-L15 is a constant (DECISION_SPEC, CONTROL_SPEC: arms, score form, sense rule, instance, X - Y order, metric, interval; bands with their arms, instances and permutations). The decisive step refuses before scoring unless spec_from_a13, which parses the terms, their order, the arm lists and the intervals from A13's own sentences (quoted verbatim from the pinned protocol file), equals the constants (check_spec). Pass 2 assembles every decision from the constants; then verify_wiring re-derives each comparison from the text's spec with its own lookup of the code files and training records, recomputes every interval and control value with stats2's and rank's functions directly, and compares them with what the decision holds; any difference stops the run with no result (WiringError). The record keeps the provenance of every comparison (its two files, instance, metric and interval), no value.

A13.11 (L14), "loss curves": every run's full curve (its recorded mean epoch losses, A10.5) is the cache's .loss.json, whose SHA-256 the run record (training, tuning-stage2.json's runs) and stage2-manifest.json (loss_files) hold and the resume check verifies; the record keeps a compact curve beside the five losses of epochs 0, 19, 99, 499 and 999: epochs 0, 10, 20, ... and the last recorded epoch (loss_curve).

A13.14, the code files "of every arm and table named in a decision of L12-L15 (the exact arms on HL, BD, WB, BD-dir, SL, MEN and WSR; the 20 measured tables on HiT test in both settings and on HL)": the exact arms' files that a decided comparison reads (the wiring's provenance, the strongest S-full and W permutations resolved; the GloVe intersections of L15(b) included) and the 20 measured tables read by G on HiT test (21 slots) and on HL within U_@, not every file a band control reads (the 20 S-full_i, W_i and GloVe-vec_i permutations); the size of each part is reported with the group's.

A13.11 (L12), "the original split file and hyperlex_rnd.tsv must agree": checked at the start of pass 2, before any HL-split metric (words, TYPE and AVG_SCORE, in order; registered: 541 noun rows in each, all covered); on a difference the run goes on (the item decides nothing), the console says so, and HL-split's values are withheld (its file metrics marked invalid, no LBENCH/1 record).

A13.13, "L14's values on the verb graph and its split (WordNet data)": the dry record shows, by whitelist, A13.11's L14 reports computed on the verb graph and its split alone (floors, the tables' macro and off-top-12 RR, G_root, the distance-only score, NK17 and F1 on the split, the Lorentz - Euclidean cells, the sign agreement and the edge-shuffle cells on the split, the exact trees on the split, Nickel & Kiela 2018's diagnostic, the relabelled tails, |dRR|); everything read on HL within U_@ stays sealed.

A13.10.5, "Tuning computes nothing else, and touches no other Stage-2 set": the tuning step makes WordNet's counts (U_@ or the verb graph, the W strata, the budget) and HiT's that need no other set (the names, the training edges, HiT val's rows, negatives and closure, and from Amendment 14's code commit on every val count of Amendment 14 item 2) and builds HiT val alone; no word column of another set, and not HiT test, is read. The decisive step makes every count of A13.9 and A13.13.

A13.16 with A13.8, the disk projection before tuning: the timing step builds the word-level instances (pass 1's readers, word fields only) and counts the code lines of the decisive run's exact plan (L12, L13, L15 and item 11), added to the learned tables' code files and the tables.

A13.14, "An amendment that changes a definition here makes stage2_protocol_v2.txt": spec_from_a13 parses Amendment 13 alone, so while a later protocol file exists the wiring check refuses rather than check the decisions against text an amendment has changed; teaching it the amending text is the definitions amendment's work.

A13.11, "every edge-shuffle cell, with 'true ≈ shuffled' where its interval does not lie above 0", and L14 control 3, "Every cell's interval is reported": the true - shuffled interval of every (geometry, d, seed) whose measured and edge-shuffled tables both exist, per metric, marked present or not; at a present seed it is control 3's own, elsewhere computed the same way and deciding nothing. The G_root and distance-only Lorentz - Euclidean cells are reported at every seed where both measured tables exist, marked; the sign agreement with G counts the present seeds (the decision's cell).

A13.13, the sealed values when a run stops: a wiring check that fails in a sealed run names each comparison, its two files, instance, metric and interval on the console and in the WiringError, with no value; the problems with their values go to a sealed side file beside the sealed file (wiring-problems.json, its SHA-256 on the console), opened after step 7 with it.

A13.11, "AP without the 3 self-pairs": the rows A13.9's count counts (BD's raw word fields equal; registered, exactly 3, else the run stops), with the N_S variant (N_S forms equal) reported beside it under its own label.
